sources.name: ACG Insights / Middle Market Growth
sources.why: Middle-market M&A, private-equity deal flow, and buy-side investment analysis — distinct dedicated dealmaking source replacing the capitalallocators.com duplicate in Corporate Finance & Dealmaking while Capital Allocators stays in Capital Allocation & Strategy.

sources.name: The Diff
sources.why: Byrne Hobart's essay series on durable competitive advantage, moats, market structure and capital-markets mechanics — first-principles strategy analysis in the Rumelt tradition, focused on the structural 'diffs' where value compounds over time.

sources.name: Continuations
sources.why: Albert Wenger's long-form essays on capital allocation, tech company strategy, and systemic market change — original first-principles analysis.

sources.name: Marginal Revolution
sources.why: Tyler Cowen and Alex Tabarrok's high-frequency economics commentary — markets, culture, empirical evidence, Freakonomics-adjacent in approach.

sources.name: Vox (The Highlight / Future Perfect)
sources.why: Accessible economics explainers and cost-benefit analysis framing — Freakonomics-style economic thinking for broad audiences.

sources.name: NBER (National Bureau of Economic Research)
sources.why: Working papers on empirical economics, behavioral finance, and market efficiency — primary-source evidence for analytical pieces.

sources.name: Duke FinReg Blog
sources.why: Duke Financial Economics Center's research-led commentary on financial regulation, banking, capital-markets and market-structure policy — dedicated financial-regulation source replacing the promarket.org duplicate in Financial Regulation & Policy while ProMarket stays in Market Structure & Competition.

sources.name: Special Situations Digest
sources.why: M&A and special-situations deal coverage with an empirical, data-driven bent — replaces the ft.com duplicate in Corporate Finance & Dealmaking while ft.com stays in Market Structure & Competition.

sources.name: ProMarket (Stigler Center, Chicago Booth)
sources.why: Chicago Booth Stigler Center's research-led commentary on competition policy, market power, antitrust and the determinants of market structure — a dedicated competition-policy source that deepens the subarea beyond M&A deal flow and FinReg reuse.

sources.name: American Antitrust Institute
sources.why: Policy analysis, amicus work and empirical research on antitrust enforcement, merger review and competitive market structure — a second dedicated market-structure/competition source giving the subarea real breadth.

sources.name: The Regulatory Review (Penn Program on Regulation)
sources.why: Penn Program on Regulation's daily commentary and scholarship on competition policy, financial market regulation, and the determinants of market structure — a distinct, feed-backed replacement for the specialsitsdigest.com and sites.duke.edu duplicates that were consolidating into their primary subareas (Corporate Finance & Dealmaking and Financial Regulation & Policy respectively). Pairs with ProMarket and the American Antitrust Institute to keep this subarea at 3 independent voices.

sources.name: Project Syndicate
sources.why: Global macro-finance analysis from leading economists (Rogoff, Rodrik, Blanchard) on systemic risk, debt, and monetary policy.

sources.name: CEPR (Centre for Economic Policy Research)
sources.why: Policy insight and discussion papers on macro-financial risk, banking resilience, and financial stability.

sources.name: NPR Planet Money
sources.why: Freakonomics-style economic storytelling on how money, markets, and monetary surprises actually work.

sources.name: Special Situations Digest
sources.why: M&A and special-situations deal coverage with an empirical, data-driven bent — replaces the ft.com duplicate in Corporate Finance & Dealmaking while ft.com stays in Market Structure & Competition.

sources.name: ACG Insights / Middle Market Growth
sources.why: Middle-market M&A, private-equity deal flow, and buy-side investment analysis — distinct dedicated dealmaking source replacing the capitalallocators.com duplicate in Corporate Finance & Dealmaking while Capital Allocators stays in Capital Allocation & Strategy.

sources.name: PE Hub
sources.why: Private-equity deal flow, leveraged buyouts, fund formation and transaction coverage — a distinct dealmaking source replacing the middlemarketgrowth.org duplicate (which stays primary in Capital Allocation & Strategy). Gives Corporate Finance & Dealmaking two independent voices alongside Special Situations Digest.

sources.name: Tax Foundation
sources.why: Deep policy analysis of how taxation shapes capital allocation, corporate investment, and market behavior.

sources.name: Duke FinReg Blog
sources.why: Duke Financial Economics Center's research-led commentary on financial regulation, banking, capital-markets and market-structure policy — dedicated financial-regulation source replacing the promarket.org duplicate in Financial Regulation & Policy while ProMarket stays in Market Structure & Competition.

sources.name: A Wealth of Common Sense
sources.why: Ben Carlson's behavioral-finance essays on investor psychology, decision-making under uncertainty, and market dynamics.

sources.name: Confessions of a Supply-Side Liberal
sources.why: Miles Kimball's essays on behavioral economics, decision-making under uncertainty, risk and welfare — rigorous Freakonomics-adjacent empirical analysis that pairs with A Wealth of Common Sense to give the behavioral subarea two distinct voices.

registries.name: OpenAlex API
registries.why: Open scholarly API for tracking new finance, economics, and strategy research papers across journals.

registries.name: SSRN
registries.why: Preprint repository for finance, economics, and corporate strategy research — early access to working papers.

registries.name: FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data)
registries.why: Comprehensive US macroeconomic time series covering rates, credit, employment, and market indicators for risk analysis.

registries.name: CEPR Discussion Papers
registries.why: Curated policy research papers on macro-finance, banking, and financial market structure.

news_vs_analysis: Balance of daily market news (FT), deep analytical essays (Project Syndicate, Stratechery, Marginal Revolution), and primary academic research (NBER, CEPR, SSRN).
notes: WSJ, Economist, Bloomberg, Reuters, HBR all bot-blocked or missing feeds — excluded. FT is primary trade-press source with free headline RSS. NBER feed is top-level working papers feed. OpenAlex API used for paper discovery bypassing journal paywalls. Freakonomics, Chamath, Rumelt domains excluded per blacklist.
